nodes.name: Admissible set
nodes.statement: A set $\mathcal{H}=\{h_1,\dotsc,h_k\}$ of distinct non-negative integers is admissible if for every prime $p$ there exists an integer $a_p$ with $a_p\not\equiv h\pmod{p}$ for all $h\in\mathcal{H}$.

nodes.name: Prime $k$-tuples conjecture
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal{H}=\{h_1,\dots,h_k\}$ be admissible. Then there are infinitely many integers $n$ such that all of $n+h_1,\dotsc,n+h_k$ are prime.
conclusions: There are infinitely many $n$ such that $n+h_1,\dotsc,n+h_k$ are all prime.

nodes.name: Level of distribution of the primes
nodes.statement: The primes have level of distribution $\theta$ if for every $A>0$, $\sum_{q\le x^\theta}\max_{(a,q)=1}\bigl|\pi(x;q,a)-\pi(x)/\phi(q)\bigr|\ll_A x/(\log x)^A$.

nodes.name: Bombieri-Vinogradov theorem
nodes.statement: The primes have level of distribution $\theta$ for every $\theta<1/2$.
conclusions: The primes have level of distribution $\theta$, in the sense of $\eqref{eq:LevelOfDistribution}$.

nodes.name: Elliott-Halberstam conjecture
nodes.statement: The primes have level of distribution $\theta$ for every $\theta<1$.
conclusions: For every $\theta<1$, $\sum_{q\le x^\theta}\max_{(a,q)=1}|\pi(x;q,a)-\pi(x)/\phi(q)|\ll_A x/(\log x)^A$ for all $A>0$.

nodes.name: Many primes in bounded intervals
nodes.statement: For every $m\in\mathbb{N}$, $\liminf_{n}(p_{n+m}-p_n)\ll m^3 e^{4m}$.

nodes.name: Positive proportion of admissible $m$-tuples satisfy prime $m$-tuples conjecture
nodes.statement: Let $m\in\mathbb{N}$ and let $r$ be sufficiently large depending on $m$. For any set $\mathcal{A}=\{a_1,\dotsc,a_r\}$ of $r$ distinct integers, $\#\{\{h_1,\dotsc,h_m\}\subseteq\mathcal{A}:\text{the prime $m$-tuples conjecture holds}\}/\binom{r}{m}\gg_m 1$.
conclusions: A positive proportion of $m$-element subsets of $\mathcal{A}$ satisfy the prime $m$-tuples conjecture.

nodes.name: Unconditional bounded gap (600)
nodes.statement: $\liminf_n(p_{n+1}-p_n)\le 600$.

nodes.name: Bounded gaps under Elliott-Halberstam
nodes.statement: Assuming the Elliott-Halberstam conjecture (level of distribution $\theta$ for every $\theta<1$), $\liminf_n(p_{n+1}-p_n)\le 12$ and $\liminf_n(p_{n+2}-p_n)\le 600$.
assumptions: The primes have level of distribution $\theta$ for every $\theta<1$ (Elliott-Halberstam).

nodes.name: Multidimensional Selberg-type sieve weights
nodes.statement: $w_n=\Bigl(\sum_{d_i\mid n+h_i\,\forall i}\lambda_{d_1,\dotsc,d_k}\Bigr)^2$ where the multidimensional weights $\lambda_{d_1,\dotsc,d_k}$ depend on each divisor individually.

nodes.name: Sums $S_1$ and $S_2$
nodes.statement: $S_1=\sum_{N\le n<2N,\ n\equiv v_0\!\!\pmod{W}}(\sum_{d_i\mid n+h_i}\lambda_{d_1,\dotsc,d_k})^2$ and $S_2=\sum_{N\le n<2N,\ n\equiv v_0\!\!\pmod{W}}(\sum_{i=1}^k\chi_{\mathbb{P}}(n+h_i))(\sum_{d_i\mid n+h_i}\lambda_{d_1,\dotsc,d_k})^2$.

nodes.name: Functionals $I_k(F)$ and $J_k^{(m)}(F)$
nodes.statement: $I_k(F)=\int_{[0,1]^k}F(t_1,\dotsc,t_k)^2\,dt$ and $J_k^{(m)}(F)=\int_{[0,1]^{k-1}}\bigl(\int_0^1 F\,dt_m\bigr)^2\prod_{i\ne m}dt_i$.

nodes.name: Maximal ratio $M_k$ and threshold $r_k$
nodes.statement: $M_k=\sup_{F\in\mathcal{S}_k}\frac{\sum_{m=1}^kJ_k^{(m)}(F)}{I_k(F)}$ and $r_k=\lceil\theta M_k/2\rceil$, where $\mathcal{S}_k$ is the set of Riemann-integrable $F:[0,1]^k\to\mathbb{R}$ supported on $\mathcal{R}_k$ with $I_k(F)\ne 0$ and $J_k^{(m)}(F)\ne 0$.

nodes.name: Simplex $\mathcal{R}_k$
nodes.statement: $\mathcal{R}_k=\{(x_1,\dotsc,x_k)\in[0,1]^k:\sum_{i=1}^kx_i\le 1\}$.

nodes.name: Change-of-variables $y_{r_1,\dotsc,r_k}$
nodes.statement: $y_{r_1,\dotsc,r_k}=\bigl(\prod_{i=1}^k\mu(r_i)\phi(r_i)\bigr)\sum_{r_i\mid d_i\,\forall i}\lambda_{d_1,\dotsc,d_k}/\prod_{i=1}^k d_i$.

nodes.name: Variables $y^{(m)}_{r_1,\dotsc,r_k}$
nodes.statement: $y^{(m)}_{r_1,\dotsc,r_k}=\bigl(\prod_{i=1}^k\mu(r_i)g(r_i)\bigr)\sum_{r_i\mid d_i\,\forall i,\ d_m=1}\lambda_{d_1,\dotsc,d_k}/\prod_{i=1}^k\phi(d_i)$, where $g$ is the totally multiplicative function with $g(p)=p-2$.

nodes.name: Smooth choice $y_{r_1,\dotsc,r_k}=F(\log r_1/\log R,\dotsc,\log r_k/\log R)$
nodes.statement: When $r=\prod r_i$ is squarefree and $(r,W)=1$, set $y_{r_1,\dotsc,r_k}=F\bigl(\log r_1/\log R,\dotsc,\log r_k/\log R\bigr)$ for a smooth $F$ supported on $\mathcal{R}_k$; otherwise zero.

nodes.name: Asymptotics for $S_1,S_2$ (Main Proposition)
nodes.statement: Suppose the primes have exponent of distribution $\theta>0$ and $R=N^{\theta/2-\delta}$. Then $S_1=(1+o(1))\phi(W)^k N(\log R)^k W^{-(k+1)} I_k(F)$ and $S_2=(1+o(1))\phi(W)^k N(\log R)^{k+1} W^{-(k+1)}(\log N)^{-1}\sum_{m=1}^k J_k^{(m)}(F)$.
assumptions: $\lambda_{d_1,\dotsc,d_k}$ as defined via smooth $F$ supported on $\mathcal{R}_k$

nodes.name: Explicit gap statement
nodes.statement: If the primes have level of distribution $\theta>0$ and $\mathcal{H}$ is admissible, then with $r_k=\lceil\theta M_k/2\rceil$ there are infinitely many $n$ such that at least $r_k$ of the $n+h_i$ are prime; in particular $\liminf_n(p_{n+r_k-1}-p_n)\le \max_{i,j}(h_i-h_j)$.
conclusions: Infinitely many $n$ have at least $r_k=\lceil\theta M_k/2\rceil$ of the $n+h_i$ prime

nodes.name: Lower bounds on $M_k$
nodes.statement: (1) $M_5>2$. (2) $M_{105}>4$. (3) For $k$ sufficiently large, $M_k>\log k-2\log\log k-2$.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 4.2
nodes.statement: Set $S=S_2-\rho S_1$; choose smooth $F_1$ approximating an extremizer of $\sum J_k^{(m)}/I_k$, apply Proposition 4.1, and pick $\rho=\theta M_k/2-\epsilon$ to force $S>0$ for all large $N$.

nodes.name: Reduce to showing $S>0$
nodes.statement: Set $S=S_2-\rho S_1$. By Section 2, $S>0$ for all large $N$ implies infinitely many $n$ have at least $\lfloor\rho+1\rfloor$ of the $n+h_i$ prime.

nodes.name: Choose near-extremizer $F_1$
nodes.statement: Pick $F_0\in\mathcal{S}_k$ with $\sum_m J_k^{(m)}(F_0)>(M_k-\delta)I_k(F_0)>0$, then approximate by smooth $F_1$ with $\sum_m J_k^{(m)}(F_1)>(M_k-2\delta)I_k(F_1)>0$.

nodes.name: Apply Proposition 4.1 and lower-bound $S$
nodes.statement: Insert the asymptotics from Proposition 4.1 to get $S\ge \phi(W)^k N(\log R)^k I_k(F_1)W^{-(k+1)}\bigl((\theta/2-\delta)(M_k-2\delta)-\rho+o(1)\bigr)$.

nodes.name: Conclude with $\rho=\theta M_k/2-\epsilon$
nodes.statement: Choose $\rho=\theta M_k/2-\epsilon$ and $\delta$ small so that $S>0$ for all large $N$; then $\lfloor\rho+1\rfloor=\lceil\theta M_k/2\rceil=r_k$, giving the conclusion.

nodes.name: Deduction of Theorems 1.1, 1.2, 1.3, 1.4 from Propositions 4.2 and 4.3
nodes.statement: By picking $k\in\{5,105\}$ or $k=\lceil C m^2 e^{4m}\rceil$ together with Engelsma's $105$-tuple of diameter $600$ (resp. $\{0,2,6,8,12\}$), Proposition 4.2 and Proposition 4.3 yield Theorems 1.1, 1.2, 1.3, 1.4.

nodes.name: Theorem 1.3: $k=105$ via Bombieri-Vinogradov
nodes.statement: Take $k=105$, $\theta=1/2-\epsilon$ (Bombieri-Vinogradov), $M_{105}>4$, hence $\theta M_{105}/2>1$; with Engelsma's $\mathcal{H}$ of diameter $600$ Proposition 4.2 gives $\liminf_n(p_{n+1}-p_n)\le 600$.

nodes.name: Theorem 1.4 (first part): $k=105$ under EH
nodes.statement: Under EH, $\theta=1-\epsilon$ and $M_{105}>4$, so $\theta M_{105}/2>2$, giving $\liminf_n(p_{n+2}-p_n)\le 600$.

nodes.name: Theorem 1.4 (second part): $k=5$ under EH
nodes.statement: Take $k=5$, $\mathcal{H}=\{0,2,6,8,12\}$ and $\theta=1-\epsilon$; $M_5>2$ gives $\theta M_5/2>1$, hence $\liminf_n(p_{n+1}-p_n)\le 12$.

nodes.name: Theorem 1.1: large $k$ asymptotic
nodes.statement: Use $\theta=1/2-\epsilon$, $M_k\ge\log k-2\log\log k-2$, and choose $k=\lceil Cm^2e^{4m}\rceil$ to obtain at least $m+1$ primes among $n+h_i$ for infinitely many $n$. Picking $\mathcal{H}=\{p_{\pi(k)+1},\dotsc,p_{\pi(k)+k}\}$ gives diameter $\ll k\log k\ll m^3 e^{4m}$.

nodes.name: Theorem 1.2: counting argument
nodes.statement: Sieve $\mathcal{A}$ to $\mathcal{A}_2$ admissible; count subsets of $\mathcal{A}_2$ of size $k$ vs size $m$ to deduce $\gg_m r^m$ admissible $m$-subsets of $\mathcal{A}$ satisfy the prime $m$-tuples conjecture.

nodes.name: Expression for $S_1$ in $y$ variables
nodes.statement: $S_1=\frac{N}{W}\sum_{r_1,\dotsc,r_k}\frac{y_{r_1,\dotsc,r_k}^2}{\prod_{i=1}^k\phi(r_i)}+O\bigl(y_{max}^2\phi(W)^k N(\log R)^k W^{-(k+1)}D_0^{-1}\bigr)$.
conclusions: The asymptotic expression above for $S_1$ in terms of $y_{r_1,\dotsc,r_k}$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 5.1
nodes.statement: Expand the square, swap summation, apply CRT, introduce divisor identity $1/[d_i,e_i]=\sum_{u_i\mid d_i,e_i}\phi(u_i)/(d_ie_i)$, remove coprimality conditions via Mobius, and substitute the change of variables to reach the diagonal sum.

nodes.name: Expand and apply CRT
nodes.statement: Expand $S_1=\sum\lambda_{d_1,\dotsc,d_k}\lambda_{e_1,\dotsc,e_k}\#\{n\equiv v_0\!\!\pmod W,\ [d_i,e_i]\mid n+h_i\}$. By CRT this is $N/q+O(1)$ when $W,[d_i,e_i]$ are pairwise coprime.

nodes.name: Decouple $d_i,e_j$ via $\phi$ identity and Mobius
nodes.statement: Use $1/[d_i,e_i]=(d_ie_i)^{-1}\sum_{u_i\mid d_i,e_i}\phi(u_i)$ and insert $\sum_{s_{i,j}\mid d_i,e_j}\mu(s_{i,j})$ to remove $(d_i,e_j)=1$ conditions.

nodes.name: Change of variables to $y_{r_1,\dotsc,r_k}$
nodes.statement: Substitute $y_{r_1,\dotsc,r_k}$ as in $\eqref{eq:YLambdaDef}$; the inverse transform $\eqref{eq:LambdaYDef}$ shows this is well-defined and $\lambda_{max}\ll y_{max}(\log R)^k$.

nodes.name: Restrict to $s_{i,j}=1$ and conclude
nodes.statement: Bound the contribution from $s_{i,j}>D_0$, dominate the negligible $R^2(\log R)^{4k}$ error using $R^2\le N^{1-2\delta}$, and obtain the diagonal expression.

nodes.name: Expression for $S_2^{(m)}$ in $y^{(m)}$ variables
nodes.statement: $S_2^{(m)}=\frac{N}{\phi(W)\log N}\sum_{r_1,\dotsc,r_k}\frac{(y^{(m)}_{r_1,\dotsc,r_k})^2}{\prod_{i=1}^k g(r_i)}+O\bigl((y^{(m)}_{max})^2\phi(W)^{k-2}N(\log N)^{k-2}W^{-(k-1)}D_0^{-1}\bigr)+O(y_{max}^2 N(\log N)^{-A})$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 5.2
nodes.statement: Expand, apply CRT, control error via Cauchy-Schwarz and the Bombieri-Vinogradov-type level-of-distribution hypothesis, then mimic the change-of-variables of Lemma 5.1 with $g(p)=p-2$ in place of $\phi(p)$.

nodes.name: Expand and apply CRT with prime-residue condition
nodes.statement: Expand $S_2^{(m)}$, apply CRT; the inner sum equals $X_N/\phi(q)+O(E(N,q))$ when $W,[d_i,e_i]$ are pairwise coprime and $d_m=e_m=1$.

nodes.name: Bound the error term via level of distribution
nodes.statement: Apply Cauchy-Schwarz with $\sum_r\mu(r)^2\tau_{3k}^2(r)/\phi(r)\ll(\log R)^{O(1)}$ and the level-of-distribution bound $\sum_r\mu(r)^2 E(N,r)\ll N(\log N)^{-A}$.

nodes.name: Decouple and substitute $y^{(m)}$
nodes.statement: Decouple $d_i,e_j$ as before, split $1/\phi([d_i,e_i])$ via $g(p)=p-2$, and substitute the variables $y^{(m)}_{r_1,\dotsc,r_k}$.

nodes.name: Apply prime number theorem and conclude
nodes.statement: Replace $X_N$ by $N/\log N+O(N/(\log N)^2)$ from PNT; the resulting error is absorbed in the main one.

nodes.name: $y^{(m)}$ in terms of $y$
nodes.statement: If $r_m=1$, then $y^{(m)}_{r_1,\dotsc,r_k}=\sum_{a_m}y_{r_1,\dotsc,r_{m-1},a_m,r_{m+1},\dotsc,r_k}/\phi(a_m)+O\bigl(y_{max}\phi(W)\log R/(W D_0)\bigr)$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 5.3
nodes.statement: Substitute $\eqref{eq:LambdaYDef}$ into the definition of $y^{(m)}$, swap summations, evaluate the divisor sums, and bound the contributions $a_j\ne r_j$ for $j\ne m$ using the constraint $a_j>D_0 r_j$.

nodes.name: Partial summation lemma (Lemma 6.1)
nodes.statement: For multiplicative $\gamma$ with $0\le\gamma(p)/p\le 1-A_1$ and average $\sum_{w\le p\le z}\gamma(p)\log p/p=\log(z/w)+O(L)+O(A_2)$, and $g(p)=\gamma(p)/(p-\gamma(p))$, $\sum_{d<z}\mu(d)^2 g(d) G(\log d/\log z)=\mathfrak{S}\log z\int_0^1 G(x)dx+O(\mathfrak{S} L G_{max})$ with $\mathfrak{S}=\prod_p (1-\gamma(p)/p)^{-1}(1-1/p)$.
assumptions: $-L\le\sum_{w\le p\le z}\gamma(p)\log p/p-\log(z/w)\le A_2$ for all $2\le w\le z$
conclusions: $\sum_{d<z}\mu(d)^2 g(d) G(\log d/\log z)=\mathfrak{S}\log z\int_0^1 G(x)\,dx+O(\mathfrak{S} L G_{max})$

nodes.name: Asymptotic for $S_1$ with smooth $F$ (Lemma 6.2)
nodes.statement: If $y_{r_1,\dotsc,r_k}=F(\log r_1/\log R,\dotsc,\log r_k/\log R)$ for smooth $F$ supported on $\mathcal{R}_k$, then $S_1=\phi(W)^k N(\log R)^k W^{-(k+1)} I_k(F)+O\bigl(F_{max}^2\phi(W)^k N(\log R)^k W^{-(k+1)} D_0^{-1}\bigr)$.
conclusions: $S_1$ matches the Main Proposition asymptotic with the explicit error bound.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 6.2
nodes.statement: Substitute the smooth $y$ into Lemma 5.1, drop the $(u_i,u_j)=1$ requirement at $D_0^{-1}$ cost, and apply Lemma 6.1 ($k$ times) with $\gamma=\mathbf{1}_{p\nmid W}$.

nodes.name: Substitute smooth $y$ into Lemma 5.1
nodes.statement: Insert $y_{r_1,\dotsc,r_k}=F(\log r_1/\log R,\dotsc,\log r_k/\log R)$ into the diagonal expression for $S_1$.

nodes.name: Drop $(u_i,u_j)=1$ at $D_0^{-1}$ cost
nodes.statement: Two integers coprime to $W$ that share a factor must share a prime $>D_0$; bound the resulting error by $F_{max}^2\phi(W)^k N(\log R)^k/(W^{k+1}D_0)$.

nodes.name: Apply Lemma 6.1 $k$ times
nodes.statement: Use $\gamma=\mathbf{1}_{p\nmid W}$ and $L\ll\log D_0$ to evaluate the inner $u_i$-sums; the result equals $\phi(W)^k(\log R)^k I_k(F)/W^k+O(\cdot)$.

nodes.name: Asymptotic for $S_2^{(m)}$ with smooth $F$ (Lemma 6.3)
nodes.statement: $S_2^{(m)}=\phi(W)^k N(\log R)^{k+1}/(W^{k+1}\log N) J_k^{(m)}(F)+O\bigl(F_{max}^2\phi(W)^k N(\log R)^k/(W^{k+1}D_0)\bigr)$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 6.3
nodes.statement: Estimate $y^{(m)}_{r_1,\dotsc,r_k}$ via Lemma 5.3 and Lemma 6.1 to obtain $y^{(m)}\approx F^{(m)}_{r_1,\dotsc,r_k}\phi(W)\log R/W$, then substitute into Lemma 5.2 and apply Lemma 6.1 $k-1$ times.

nodes.name: Beta-function integration over $\mathcal{R}_k$ (Lemma 7.1)
nodes.section: 7 Choice of smooth weight for large $k$ (Lemma 7.1)
nodes.statement: $\int_{\mathcal{R}_k}(1-P_1)^a P_j^b\,dt_1\dotsc dt_k=\frac{a!}{(k+jb+a)!} G_{b,j}(k)$, where $G_{b,j}(x)=b!\sum_{r=1}^b\binom{x}{r}\sum_{b_1+\dotsb+b_r=b,\ b_i\ge 1}\prod_i (jb_i)!/b_i!$ depends only on $b,j$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 7.1
nodes.statement: Induct on $k$ to establish $\int_{\mathcal{R}_k}(1-\sum t_i)^a\prod t_i^{a_i}=a!\prod a_i!/(k+a+\sum a_i)!$ via the beta identity, then expand $P_j^b$ multinomially and split by the number $r$ of nonzero exponents.

nodes.name: Inductive evaluation of monomial integral
nodes.statement: Show by induction on $k$ that $\int_{\mathcal{R}_k}(1-\sum t_i)^a\prod t_i^{a_i}\,dt=a!\prod a_i!/(k+a+\sum a_i)!$, using the substitution $v=t_1/(1-\sum_{i\ge 2}t_i)$ and the beta identity.

nodes.name: Expand $P_j^b$ via multinomial
nodes.statement: $P_j^b=\sum_{b_1+\dotsb+b_k=b} b!/\prod b_i! \prod t_i^{jb_i}$; integrate term-by-term using Step 1.

nodes.name: Split by number of nonzero exponents
nodes.statement: Group monomials by the number $r$ of nonzero $b_i$ to write $\sum_{b_1,\dotsc,b_k}\dotsb=\sum_r\binom{k}{r}\sum_{b_1,\dotsc,b_r\ge 1}\dotsb$, yielding $G_{b,j}(k)$.

nodes.name: Quadratic form expressions for $I_k$ and $J_k^{(m)}$ (Lemma 8.1)
nodes.statement: If $P=\sum_i a_i (1-P_1)^{b_i} P_2^{c_i}$, then $I_k(F)$ and $J_k^{(m)}(F)$ are positive-definite quadratic forms in $\mathbf{a}$ with explicit rational coefficients in terms of the polynomials $G_{\cdot,2}$.
assumptions: $F$ as in $\eqref{eq:FChoice}$ given by polynomial $P=\sum_i a_i(1-P_1)^{b_i}P_2^{c_i}$
conclusions: $J_k^{(m)}(F)$ has the explicit double-sum form given in the paper.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 8.1
nodes.statement: Apply Lemma 7.1 to evaluate $I_k(F)=\int_{\mathcal{R}_k}P^2$, and reduce $J_k^{(m)}(F)$ via inner integration $\int_0^{1-\sum_{i\ge 2}t_i}(1-P_1)^b P_2^c dt_1$, expanding $P_2^c$ binomially and applying Lemma 7.1 over $\mathcal{R}_{k-1}$.

nodes.name: Generalized Rayleigh quotient via eigenvalues (Lemma 8.2)
nodes.statement: For real symmetric positive-definite $A_1,A_2$, $\mathbf{a}^T A_2 \mathbf{a}/\mathbf{a}^T A_1 \mathbf{a}$ is maximized when $\mathbf{a}$ is a top eigenvector of $A_1^{-1}A_2$, with maximal value the largest eigenvalue.
conclusions: $\max\mathbf{a}^T A_2\mathbf{a}/\mathbf{a}^T A_1\mathbf{a}$ equals the largest eigenvalue of $A_1^{-1}A_2$, attained at the corresponding eigenvector.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 8.2
nodes.statement: Normalize $\mathbf{a}^T A_1\mathbf{a}=1$ and apply Lagrange multipliers: stationarity gives $A_1^{-1}A_2\mathbf{a}=\lambda\mathbf{a}$, with $\mathbf{a}^T A_2\mathbf{a}=\lambda$.

nodes.name: GPY weights of Goldston-Pintz-Yildirim
nodes.statement: $\lambda_d=\mu(d)F(\log R/d)$ for a smooth function $F$; with $F(x)=x^{k+l}$ this is essentially optimal for large $k$.

nodes.name: Approximate form of multidimensional weights
nodes.statement: $\lambda_{d_1,\dotsc,d_k}\approx \bigl(\prod_i\mu(d_i)\bigr) f(d_1,\dotsc,d_k)$ for a suitable smooth $f$.

nodes.name: Definition of $\lambda_{d_1,\dotsc,d_k}$ in terms of smooth $F$
nodes.statement: $\lambda_{d_1,\dotsc,d_k}=\bigl(\prod_i\mu(d_i)d_i\bigr)\sum_{d_i\mid r_i,\ (r_i,W)=1}\mu(\prod_i r_i)^2/\prod_i\phi(r_i)\cdot F(\log r_1/\log R,\dotsc,\log r_k/\log R)$ when $(\prod d_i,W)=1$, else zero.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 4.3 part (3) (large $k$)
nodes.section: 7 Choice of smooth weight for large $k$
nodes.statement: Construct $F(t_1,\dotsc,t_k)=\prod_i g(kt_i)$ on $\mathcal{R}_k$ for $g(t)=1/(1+At)$ on $[0,T]$ with $1+AT=e^A$ and $A=\log k-2\log\log k$; concentration of measure shows $kJ_k/I_k\ge A(1-O(1/(\log k)^2))\ge\log k-2\log\log k-2$.

nodes.name: Choose product form $F=\prod g(kt_i)$
nodes.statement: Take $F(t_1,\dotsc,t_k)=\prod_{i=1}^k g(kt_i)\mathbf{1}_{\sum t_i\le 1}$ for smooth $g:[0,T]\to\mathbb{R}$. By symmetry $J_k^{(m)}=J_k$ for all $m$.

nodes.name: Bound $I_k\le k^{-k}\gamma^k$ and $J_k\ge J_k'-E_k$
nodes.statement: Use $I_k\le(\int g(kt)^2dt)^k=k^{-k}\gamma^k$. Restrict the $J_k$ outer integral to $\sum_{i\ge 2}t_i\le 1-T/k$ to free the inner integral and write the bound as $J_k'-E_k$.

nodes.name: Concentration-of-measure bound on $E_k$
nodes.statement: If the center of mass $\mu$ of $g^2$ satisfies $\mu<1-T/k$, set $\eta=(k-T)/(k-1)-\mu$ and use Chebyshev: $E_k\le\eta^{-2}\mu T k^{-k-1}\gamma^{k-1}(\int g)^2/(k-1)$.

nodes.name: Optimize over $g$ via Euler-Lagrange
nodes.statement: Maximize $\int g$ subject to $\int g^2=\gamma$, $\int u g^2=\mu\gamma$; Lagrange multipliers give $g(t)=1/(2\alpha+2\beta t)$, so WLOG $g(t)=1/(1+At)$ on $[0,T]$.

nodes.name: Choose $1+AT=e^A$ and $A=\log k-2\log\log k$
nodes.statement: With $1+AT=e^A$, $\mu=1/(1-e^{-A})-1/A$ and $T\le e^A/A$. Setting $A=\log k-2\log\log k$, the constraint $\mu<1-T/k$ holds for large $k$.

nodes.name: Conclude $M_k\ge\log k-2\log\log k-2$
nodes.statement: Substituting back yields $kJ_k/I_k\ge A(1-A e^A/(k(1-A/(e^A-1)-e^A/k)^2))\ge\log k-2\log\log k-2$ for $k$ large.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 4.3 parts (1) and (2) (small $k$)
nodes.statement: Take $F$ a polynomial in $P_1,P_2$; use Lemma 8.1 to write $\sum J_k^{(m)}/I_k=\mathbf{a}^T A_2\mathbf{a}/\mathbf{a}^T A_1\mathbf{a}$ and Lemma 8.2 to maximize. For $k=105$ and $b+2c\le 11$ (42 monomials), the largest eigenvalue $\lambda\approx 4.0020697>4$. For $k=5$ and an explicit $P$, $\sum J_5^{(m)}/I_5=1417255/708216>2$.

nodes.name: Reduce to generalized eigenvalue problem
nodes.statement: Restrict $F=P\mathbf{1}_{\mathcal{R}_k}$ for symmetric polynomial $P=\sum_i a_i(1-P_1)^{b_i}P_2^{c_i}$; by Lemma 8.1, $\sum_m J_k^{(m)}(F)/I_k(F)=\mathbf{a}^T A_2\mathbf{a}/\mathbf{a}^T A_1\mathbf{a}$ for explicit rational symmetric positive-definite $A_1,A_2$.

nodes.name: $k=105$: compute top eigenvalue numerically
nodes.statement: With monomials $(1-P_1)^bP_2^c$, $b+2c\le 11$ (42 monomials), the $42\times 42$ matrices $A_1,A_2$ at $k=105$ give the largest eigenvalue of $A_1^{-1}A_2$ as $\lambda\approx 4.0020697>4$, so $M_{105}>4$.

nodes.name: Engelsma's 105-tuple of diameter 600
nodes.statement: An explicit admissible $\mathcal{H}=\{0,10,12,\dotsc,600\}$ of size $105$ with diameter $h_{105}-h_1=600$, computed by Thomas Engelsma; used in Theorems 1.3 and 1.4.

nodes.name: Admissible 5-tuple $\{0,2,6,8,12\}$
nodes.statement: $\mathcal{H}=\{0,2,6,8,12\}$ is admissible with diameter $12$; used in the EH part of Theorem 1.4 to conclude $\liminf_n(p_{n+1}-p_n)\le 12$.

nodes.name: Set of $k$ primes greater than $k$
nodes.statement: Take $\mathcal{H}=\{p_{\pi(k)+1},\dotsc,p_{\pi(k)+k}\}$, the first $k$ primes exceeding $k$; this is admissible and has diameter $\ll k\log k$, used to prove Theorem 1.1.

nodes.name: Tao's parallel approach
nodes.statement: Terence Tao has independently proved Theorem 1.1 (with a slightly weaker bound) at much the same time, using a similar method but with calculations done via Fourier integrals on $\lambda_{d_1,\dotsc,d_k}\approx(\prod\mu(d_i))f(d_1,\dotsc,d_k)$.

nodes.name: Effective bounds via exceptional moduli
nodes.statement: Restricting $\lambda_{d_1,\dotsc,d_k}$ to be supported on $d_i$ coprime to the largest prime factor of a possible exceptional modulus yields effective implied constants, at the cost of a negligible error.

nodes.name: Reduction to GPY when $F$ depends only on $\sum t_i$
nodes.statement: When $F(t_1,\dotsc,t_k)=G(\sum_i t_i)$, $I_k(F)$ and $J_k^{(m)}(F)$ reduce to $\int_0^1 G(t)^2 t^{k-1}dt/(k-1)!$ and $\int_0^1(\int_t^1 G(v)dv)^2 t^{k-2}dt/(k-2)!$, recovering the original GPY-method results.

nodes.name: Eigenfunction interpretation of optimal $F$
nodes.section: 7 Choice of smooth weight for large $k$
nodes.statement: An optimal $F$ for $\sum_m J_k^{(m)}(F)/I_k(F)$ is expected to be an eigenfunction of the operator $\mathcal{L}_k F(u_1,\dotsc,u_k)=\sum_m\int_0^{1-\sum_{i\ne m}u_i}F(u_1,\dotsc,t_m,\dotsc,u_k)dt_m$, with eigenvalue equal to the maximal ratio. The eigenvalue equation is unsolved for $k>2$.
